const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-preferred-design-luna.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

The grouping policy already builds connected components from exact-name evidence and reviewed BBC/GB News/Premier League families, then stores minimum-UUID representatives in `funder_alias_groups`. That UUID must remain the stable group identity. Choosing a display name from that representative is accidental: an alias bridge can make an unrelated recorded name the representative, and singletons still need ordinary canonical names. The preferred label must be derived from the complete component after all joins, be searchable even when no source funder records it, and leave source names, aliases, evidence, and member history untouched.

## Usage (caller's view)

`search_funders("bbc")` returns the stable group id, label `BBC`, and the winning name/alias source. `funder_details(group_id)` returns the same label plus `display_name_basis = reviewed_family("bbc")`; its aliases and evidence remain exact source data. `member_history(member_id)` continues to show each recorded funder name for each source occurrence.

## Shape

Persist one pipeline-owned projection row per component in a new `exposed.funder_group_names` table: `group_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES exposed.funders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `preferred_name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (btrim(preferred_name) <> '')`, and nullable `reviewed_family_key TEXT`. A null key means the label is the representative's canonical recorded name; a non-null key identifies the reviewed policy that supplied the label. A row is written for every component, including singletons. Add a reversible SQLx migration pair. This is presentation metadata keyed by existing group identity; do not alter `funder_alias_groups` or member records.

Extend policy entries to `{key, names, preferred_name}` and parse `preferred_name` into a nonempty `PreferredFunderName` boundary type. While constructing `FunderGroups`, first finish all exact and family unions, then collect reviewed family keys represented by each final component. If exactly one reviewed key occurs, project that family's preferred name and key; if none occur, project the representative's canonical name and null key. If multiple distinct keys occur in one component (for example, an alias bridge joins reviewed families), fail the refresh as ambiguous instead of silently choosing a label. This keeps ambiguity visible and refresh atomic. Duplicate normalized policy names remain rejected.

```rust
pub struct PreferredFunderName(String); // parse: trim, reject empty
pub struct GroupDisplayName {
    pub group_id: FunderId,
    pub name: PreferredFunderName,
    pub basis: DisplayNameBasis,
}
pub enum DisplayNameBasis { RecordedRepresentative, ReviewedFamily(String) }
pub struct FunderGroups { memberships: Vec<(FunderId,FunderId)>, display_names: Vec<GroupDisplayName>, alias_links: ..., family_links: ... }
fn build_funder_groups(funders: &[GroupingFunder]) -> Result<FunderGroups, FunderGroupingError>; // pure policy/domain
```

In `outbound/funder_grouping.rs::replace_funder_groups`, insert memberships/evidence and then `DELETE`/insert the complete `funder_group_names` projection inside the existing advisory-locked transaction. Use `sqlx::query!` for writes. Singletons are already in memberships, so this projection is total. Any policy ambiguity rolls back the old projection intact.

In `outbound/funder.rs`, join candidates to membership then `funder_group_names`; union the stored preferred name into text candidates, score it with `word_similarity`, and group by the existing `group_id` while returning the display name and its basis. Do the same for the display candidate in phonetic search if its label can be a person's name; reviewed organization labels currently do not need phonetic matching, so keep phonetic ranking over recorded names and substitute the stored display label only in the returned funder. Add a `SearchMatchSource::PreferredName` (or equivalent explicit basis) when the winning candidate is the synthetic reviewed label. In `entity_details.rs::funder_funding`, fetch label and basis by `group_id` for the profile while retaining aliases, link evidence, and the existing `e.funder_id = ANY(member_ids)` history query. Member details continue joining `e.funder_id` directly to `funders`.

The public surface adds only typed display provenance to funder search/profile results; SQL grouping and policy parsing remain behind the existing repository/domain boundaries. This hides component aggregation from callers and keeps source observations distinct from curated presentation.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate recommendation: persist the post-union group-name projection. The existing membership projection already establishes group identity and atomic refresh ownership, so this adds one compact, queryable output without changing identity semantics.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept one persisted row per singleton and group in exchange for total, simple reads and no runtime policy/component reconstruction.
- We accept rejecting a refresh when reviewed-family labels become ambiguous in exchange for never publishing a misleading label; old projection survives because refresh is transactional.
- We accept duplicating the policy's chosen label in the projection in exchange for search and details using one consistent current value.

## Alternatives considered

- Put `preferred_name` on each membership: loses a single owner for the label, repeats the same metadata N times, and allows rows in one component to disagree; reads and writes become more exposed to callers.
- Look up policy at query time: hides no component resolution complexity, cannot reliably account for alias bridges/singletons, and couples search/details to policy-file parsing on every read.
- Add a new canonical funder row or rewrite source funder names: corrupts source identity/evidence and can change the minimum-UUID group id.

## Implementation reconciliation

Not implemented.

## Open questions and risks

Should a component containing two reviewed keys fail refresh as designed, or should policy provide an explicit precedence rule? The former has the safer default and forces a reviewer to resolve the policy conflict.

## Next implementation step

Add preferred labels to the versioned policy and make the pure grouping builder return one validated display-name projection per final component, including singleton tests.
EOF",yield_time_ms:10000,max_output_tokens:2000});
